quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Where should you place a load on your motorcycle?

options.text: As low as possible
As high as possible
Behind the rear axle
On one side of the motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible
questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure them in saddlebags. Piling loads high on the back raises your motorcycle's center of gravity and changes how it balances. Always spread weight equally on both sides.

questions.question: What should you do when it is raining?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off to the side of the road until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Increase your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Wet roads are slippery, especially when rain just starts. Oil deposits from cars stay on the road at first. Riding in the tire tracks cars leave is safer. The left tire track is usually your best choice.

questions.question: How do you regain control if your rear tire locks up?

options.text: Release the rear brake.
Continue using the rear brake.
Swerve the bike in the direction with the fewest hazards.
With the brake engaged, try to accelerate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the rear brake.
questions.explanation: To regain control when the rear wheel locks, release the rear brake. If you lock the rear brake on dry pavement, you can keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: What should you do to stop quickly?

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Use both brakes.
Use the rear brake firmly while gradually increasing the braking pressure of the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: What must an eye or face shield do to be effective?

options.text: Fasten securely.
Prevent air from passing through.
Not allow for eyeglasses to fit underneath.
Restrict your vision to the sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fasten securely.
questions.explanation: An effective shield must be free of scratches, resist breaking, give clear side vision, fasten securely, allow air to prevent fogging, and fit over eyeglasses if needed.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Where should you ride to have the most room for error if a passing vehicle creates a wind blast?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the center portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Riding in the middle of your lane gives you the most room to recover if a wind blast affects your control.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: The left position in the lane
The center position in the lane
The right position in the lane
There is no single lane position that is best for all situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single lane position that is best for all situations.
questions.explanation: No lane position is always best. Choose a position based on road conditions that lets you keep safe distance and stay visible to others.

questions.question: Should you use your headlight during the day?

options.text: Not be used.
Be used on its high beam setting.
Be used on its low beam setting.
Alternate between high beam and low beam settings.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be used on its high beam setting.
questions.explanation: Use your high beam headlight during the day. It helps other drivers see you. Use high beam anytime you are not behind or approaching other vehicles.

questions.question: What formation should a group of three-wheel motorcycles use?

options.text: Staggered formation.
Pyramid formation.
Single-file line.
Row of pairs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file line.
questions.explanation: Two-wheel motorcycles use staggered formations, but three-wheel motorcycles are too wide. A group of three-wheel motorcycles should travel in a single-file line.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheeled motorcycle through a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the center of the lane.
Stay on the outside of the lane.
Change your path as needed.
Use the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your path as needed.
questions.explanation: Three-wheeled motorcycles and motorcycles with sidecars turn differently than two-wheeled motorcycles. You may need to move from the outside of the curve to the inside before straightening out your path.

questions.question: Swerving a motorcycle requires what?

options.text: Requires a lot of traction.
Requires little traction.
Is a slow maneuver.
Should be done to avoid a hazard on a slippery road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Requires a lot of traction.
questions.explanation: Swerving is a quick move that needs a lot of traction to do safely. Do not swerve suddenly on slippery roads.

questions.question: If your throttle gets stuck, what should you do?

options.text: Jump off the motorcycle.
Apply the brakes.
Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
Not try to twist the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
questions.explanation: If your throttle is stuck, twist it back and forth several times to free it. If that does not work, use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch at the same time.

questions.question: A helmet should not:

options.text: Meet U.S. DOT standards.
Fit snugly.
Be without obvious defects.
Have been worn in a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have been worn in a crash.
questions.explanation: A good helmet should meet U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards, fit snugly all the way around, and have no obvious defects. Replace any helmet that was worn during a crash.

questions.question: The center portion of a lane often has an oily strip. This strip:

options.text: Is not safe for motorcyclists at any time.
Is usually safe for motorcyclists, unless it is raining.
Should always be avoided since other parts of the lane do not have the oily strip.
Adds to traction for most motorcycle tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is usually safe for motorcyclists, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: Oil drips from cars and collects in the center of the lane. The road usually provides enough traction for motorcycles to ride safely here unless it is wet. Since the strip is often less than two feet wide, you can ride to one side of it and still stay in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: When choosing a lane position, what should you do?

options.text: Always ride in the center portion of the lane.
Always ride in the left portion of the lane.
Always ride in the right portion of the lane.
Be flexible and base your decision on many different factors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be flexible and base your decision on many different factors.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Choose the part of the lane where you are most likely to be seen and can keep space around you.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Avoid other drivers' blind spots.
Avoid surface hazards.
Block your access to an escape route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block your access to an escape route.
questions.explanation: A good lane position should help you see others and be seen. It should keep you away from wind blasts, other drivers' blind spots, and surface hazards. Your lane position should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and should give you an escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: If you are preparing to pass another rider on the left, what should you do?

options.text: Get into the right part of the lane so you can be seen in their side mirror.
Get into the left part of the lane to increase your line of sight.
Stay in the center part of the lane so you can be seen in their rearview mirror.
Weave in your lane to draw attention to yourself.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get into the left part of the lane to increase your line of sight.
questions.explanation: When passing a vehicle on its left, ride in the left portion of your lane to see better and be more visible. Check your mirrors and turn your head to look for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should you not do?

options.text: Ride more slowly than you would normally.
Start slowing earlier than you would normally.
Increase your following distance.
Talk to your passenger while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Talk to your passenger while riding.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight, so your motorcycle will slow down more gradually. Ride slower than normal, start slowing sooner, and stay farther behind other vehicles. Always let your passenger know about upcoming conditions.

questions.question: Your lane position should not:

options.text: Increase your ability to see.
Avoid placing you in other drivers' blind spots.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Provide you with an escape route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position should help you see others and be seen. It should keep you away from wind blasts, other drivers' blind spots, and surface hazards. Your lane position should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and should give you an escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: What should you do if your front tire locks while braking?

options.text: Keep the brake engaged until you stop completely.
Release both brakes and let the bike coast to a stop.
Release the brake lever and use only the rear brake.
Release the brake lever until the tire grips the road again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the brake lever until the tire grips the road again.
questions.explanation: If your front tire locks while braking, release the brake lever until the tire grips the road again. Then apply the brake again.

questions.question: As weight shifts forward to the front of your bike while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Slowly increase pressure on the front brake.
Use more rear brake pressure.
Do nothing. Weight transfer will not affect your motorcycle.
Try to lock the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly increase pressure on the front brake.
questions.explanation: While braking, slowly increase the pressure on the front brake lever as the bike's weight moves forward to the front tire.

questions.question: Why should you not move to the far side of your lane when being passed?

options.text: The passing vehicle may come back into your lane too soon.
You may block another vehicle from passing you.
The side closest to the passing vehicle is safer.
You will feel more wind blast on the far side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The passing vehicle may come back into your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: When being passed, do not ride on the far side of your lane. This may encourage the passing driver to return to your lane before it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What is the best protection for a motorcycle rider?

options.text: Keeping space between your bike and other vehicles.
Wearing a good leather jacket.
Wearing sturdy boots.
Knowing motorcycle laws well.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeping space between your bike and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Your best protection against crashes is to keep distance from other vehicles. Space gives you time to react if other drivers make mistakes. Wearing proper protective gear is also important.

questions.question: When riding at night, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Use your high beam.
Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.
Make yourself visible.
Ride only in the left side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride only in the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, use your high beam (unless meeting or following another vehicle), use other vehicles' headlights to help you see, and wear reflective clothing. Change your lane position as needed to see better, be seen, and stay safe.
